pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks seeded rows are all 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
src/index.js item() prefixes '★ ' only when starred; 'AC-2' test expects the exact list with only item 2 marked.
VIEWS.starred filters WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id; 'AC-3' stars 3 then 1 and expects id order, status 200.
'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all both return all three items in id order with the star on item 3.
'AC-5' asserts the exact 'Starred only' link on / and the 'All items' link on the starred view.
Object.hasOwn(VIEWS, show) check returns 400; 'AC-6' covers Starred, none, empty and __proto__ and asserts no <li>.

traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'; 'AC-7' asserts it. The checker script accepts queries and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers it. The traffic worker passes the path straight into the URL, so the query is requested.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec. The decisions are followed: id order is kept and the view is a query parameter. Nothing is added beyond the spec except the checker's query-string allowance, which AC-7 needs, and the PR discloses it.

All 7 acceptance items are implemented and named by tests. Each of the four state-table rows has a test checking the list, the message and the link. The spec has no late edits; its commit is part of the change with the go dated.

The tests run real requests against local D1 and would fail if the code were wrong. test/apply-migrations.js resets the database before each test. I could not run them here because vitest is not installed (npm test: vitest not found); CI runs them. The traffic fake-app change only widens what it records, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh adds negative cases for '#' and spaces.
README describes ?show=starred. The routes.json instruction is already there and the change follows it.
The SQL is built only from fixed VIEWS entries, never from user input. Object.hasOwn blocks prototype keys. An empty or repeated show value is handled: the first value is used, and empty gives 400.
The show value is whitelisted, titles are HTML-escaped, and the SQL is static. No instructions in the repo tried to steer the review.
Only a minimal server-rendered HTML page changed. The diff has no CSS, components or other UI files, and there are no screenshots to judge.
No UI flow could be run here: there is no browser and the tests cannot run in this environment.
The title is under 72 characters. The claims match the diff: migration, 400 on other values, route check change, and the fake-app change disclosed as not loosening anything.
